## Two papers, complementary contributions {#two-papers}

<div class="sparsev-papers">
  <article class="sparsev-paper" id="paper">
    <div class="sparsev-paper-label">01 · SEM · DISCRIMINATION</div>
    <h3>Simulation-cum-ROC fit evaluation in sparse ordinal CFA under category collapsing</h3>
    <p class="sparsev-paper-question">Can fit indices distinguish correct from misspecified CFA models?</p>
    <div class="sparsev-paper-outcome"><span>ROC / AUC</span><span>Detection</span><span>Category collapsing</span></div>
    <p class="sparsev-citation"><strong>Liu, L.</strong>, Liu, J., Yi, H., &amp; Okech, D. (2026). <em>Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal</em>.</p>
    <div class="sparsev-paper-links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2026.2691170">Published paper ↗</a><a href="https://osf.io/b7atw/" id="code">Code / OSF ↗</a></div>
  </article>
  <article class="sparsev-paper" id="brm-paper">
    <div class="sparsev-paper-label">02 · BRM · CALIBRATION</div>
    <h3>Calibrating fit-index cutoffs for sparse ordinal CFA: Scenario-specific thresholds and operating characteristics</h3>
    <p class="sparsev-paper-question">How should cutoffs be calibrated for a given analysis scenario?</p>
    <div class="sparsev-paper-outcome"><span>Tail-quantile cutoffs</span><span>False rejection</span><span>Detection</span></div>
    <p class="sparsev-citation"><strong>Liu, L.</strong>, Liu, J., &amp; Okech, D. (2026). <em>Behavior Research Methods, 58</em>, Article 341.</p>
    <div class="sparsev-paper-links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-026-03221-8">Published paper ↗</a><a href="https://osf.io/ce7rm/">Code &amp; data / OSF ↗</a></div>
  </article>
</div>

## Simulation design {#simulation-design}

<div class="sparsev-design-strip">
<div><span>ESTIMATORS</span><strong>MLR · MLMV · WLSMV</strong></div>
<div><span>FIT INDICES</span><strong>CFI · TLI · RMSEA · SRMR</strong></div>
<div><span>BRM SAMPLE SIZES</span><strong>250 · 500 · 1,000</strong></div>
<div><span>CATEGORY HANDLING</span><strong>Original · Collapsed</strong></div>
</div>

<figure class="sparsev-figure sparsev-models">
<div class="sparsev-figure-label">THREE FITTED-MODEL CONDITIONS</div>
<div class="sparsev-model-grid">
  <div class="sparsev-model">
    <span class="sparsev-model-type">CORRECT</span>
    <div class="sparsev-model-nodes"><i>F1</i><i>F2</i><i>F3</i></div>
    <strong>Cross-loading retained</strong>
    <small>Reference for cutoff calibration</small>
  </div>
  <div class="sparsev-model">
    <span class="sparsev-model-type">LOCAL MISFIT</span>
    <div class="sparsev-model-nodes"><i>F1</i><i>F2</i><i>F3</i></div>
    <strong>Cross-loading omitted</strong>
    <small>Localized departure</small>
  </div>
  <div class="sparsev-model">
    <span class="sparsev-model-type">SEVERE MISFIT</span>
    <div class="sparsev-model-nodes"><i class="sparsev-merged">F1 + F2</i><i>F3</i></div>
    <strong>Two factors combined</strong>
    <small>Stronger structural departure</small>
  </div>
</div>
<figcaption>Conceptual model comparison, not estimated path diagrams. BRM calibrates on the Correct model and evaluates detection under the misspecified models.</figcaption>
</figure>

## What the results show {#key-findings}

<figure class="sparsev-figure sparsev-result">
<div class="sparsev-figure-label">BRM · CFI–RMSEA AND RULE · MODERATE LOADINGS</div>
<div class="sparsev-result-grid">
  <div class="sparsev-bar-row"><div class="sparsev-bar-head"><strong>False rejection</strong><b>8.0%</b></div><div class="sparsev-track"><span style="width:8%" class="sparsev-bar-neutral"></span></div><small>Correctly specified model</small></div>
  <div class="sparsev-bar-row"><div class="sparsev-bar-head"><strong>Local misfit detection</strong><b>39.1%</b></div><div class="sparsev-track"><span style="width:39.1%"></span></div><small>Omitted cross-loading</small></div>
  <div class="sparsev-bar-row"><div class="sparsev-bar-head"><strong>Severe misfit detection</strong><b>90.3%</b></div><div class="sparsev-track"><span style="width:90.3%"></span></div><small>Combined factors</small></div>
</div>
<figcaption>Scenario-level means across BRM moderate-loading conditions. These results describe the studied designs, not universal decision-rule performance.</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sparsev-insights">
<div><span>01</span><strong>Cutoffs depend on context</strong><small>Estimator, sample size, loadings, and sparsity all matter.</small></div>
<div><span>02</span><strong>Local misfit is harder to detect</strong><small>Detection is lower than for severe misfit.</small></div>
<div><span>03</span><strong>Collapsing is not uniformly beneficial</strong><small>BRM found larger WLSMV detection gains in lower-information settings.</small></div>
</div>

## Applied illustration {#applied-illustration}

<p class="sparsev-section-intro">Sierra Leone household welfare scale · <strong>6 items</strong> · <strong>N = 2,989</strong> · BRM</p>

<figure class="sparsev-figure sparsev-example">
<div class="sparsev-figure-label">ORIGINAL VS. COLLAPSED RESPONSE SCALE</div>
<div class="sparsev-example-grid">
  <div class="sparsev-example-side">
    <span class="sparsev-example-label">ORIGINAL · FIVE CATEGORIES</span>
    <div class="sparsev-scale"><span>1</span><span>2</span><span>3</span><span>4</span><span>5</span></div>
    <div class="sparsev-example-metric"><strong>5 / 6</strong><small>Items with sparse categories</small></div>
    <div class="sparsev-example-metric"><strong>13</strong><small>Zero bivariate cells</small></div>
    <div class="sparsev-example-rmsea"><div><span>Observed RMSEA</span><strong>.079</strong></div><div class="sparsev-track"><span style="width:79%"></span></div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="sparsev-example-divider" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
  <div class="sparsev-example-side">
    <span class="sparsev-example-label">COLLAPSED · THREE CATEGORIES</span>
    <div class="sparsev-scale sparsev-three"><span>1–2</span><span>3</span><span>4–5</span></div>
    <div class="sparsev-example-metric"><strong>0 / 6</strong><small>Items with sparse categories</small></div>
    <div class="sparsev-example-metric"><strong>0</strong><small>Zero bivariate cells</small></div>
    <div class="sparsev-example-rmsea"><div><span>Observed RMSEA</span><strong>.057</strong></div><div class="sparsev-track"><span style="width:57%"></span></div></div>
  </div>
</div>
<figcaption>RMSEA bars share a 0–.10 scale. Collapsing removed sparse-cell diagnostics and reduced RMSEA, but both versions fell on the worse-fit side of their respective model-conditional calibrated cutoffs. A conventional .06 benchmark would classify them differently.</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sparsev-end-note"><strong>Research contribution.</strong> The two papers connect fit-index <em>discrimination</em> with scenario-calibrated <em>decisions</em> for sparse ordinal measurement.</div>
